Review this screen as the studio's UX reviewer: Charlie, main navigation (top section tabs) at 390 and 1280, restyle PR https://github.com/holroydchase-afk/charlie/pull/49 (Nov 21, 2026).

Give a score out of 10 and your findings with priorities (P0 to P2). Say what you would check that a pass could miss.
rubric: Pass only if the reply raises this problem, which a past review missed: The owner opened it the same day and said the tabs "read like a website, not an app." A re-review of navigation against the design system scored it 5/10 ("a marketing site with an app stapled under it"): the section links are underlined text that scroll away, the pinned brand bar has no navigation on it, and there is no bottom bar on phones or sidebar on laptops. The reviewer judged the restyle's visuals but never asked whether the app felt like an app.

Give a score out of 10 and your findings with priorities (P0 to P2). Say what you would check that a pass could miss.
rubric: Pass only if the reply raises this problem, which a past review missed: A phone's first screen shows no idea. The Nov 17 live-demo review found the first idea card about 785px down (UX-L3, P2), and the Nov 21 navigation re-review measured it at 808px, behind the fixed footer, because Today opens like a landing page (hero pitch first). Fix proposed: a plain "Today" title and no hero, which brings the first card to about 470px. A jump link to content that isn't visible was graded as solving "ideas above the fold".

The earlier reviews checked that the disclaimer was present, not what the reply looked like to a reader.

text:
Review this screen as the studio's UX reviewer: ccwatts playground Overview roll-up and its detail tabs (Electricity, Pace, Share, Method) on the studio design system. ccwatts PR #102 final round, merged and live Nov 22, 2026.

Give a score out of 10 and your findings with priorities (P0 to P2). Say what you would check that a pass could miss.
rubric: Pass only if the reply raises this problem, which a past review missed: A few hours after it went live, Chase called the product "very busy", with high information density and the most important points and CTAs hard to find. The next ux-reviewer showcase pass scored it 5/10 on phone and 6/10 on laptop for main point and CTA. It found no main button in the first viewport at either width, an Overview that was a five-row menu repeating the tabs, a header with four layers (about 270 of 844px) and the privacy promise stated twice on laptop, an Electricity tab with seven equal-weight sections (2,294px tall on phone), four equal buttons on Share with receipt text at about 4px, and numbers with no range or method version (64%, 28 miles, 5.7 days, model percentages), which breaks a ccwatts hard rule.
